clue.text: Wife gave wonga so was giddy

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for wife
to heel is to supply with money, as in well-heeled; wonga is British slang for cash

explanation.surface: A husband hands over cash and his wife is dizzy with delight.
explanation.walkthrough: Wonga is British slang for money; heel in the sense of providing funds survives mainly in 'well-heeled'.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel can mean to reel or spin round, so a person who wheeled felt dizzy and turned about unsteadily.

clue.text: Prince packing weight to twist in a rare way

definitions.text: to twist in a rare way

indicators.note: packing here means the prince is packed into the weight abbreviation

blocks.note: the first part of WT, the abbreviation for weight
a ras is an Ethiopian prince
the rest of WT, the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: A prince carrying a weight twists it in an unusual way.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrast is an obsolete form of wrest, meaning to wrench or twist; 'in a rare way' marks the uncommon form.

clue.text: Caviar places, perhaps, cherish tea that’s served up

indicators.note: served up means dished out in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the ten letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: People who love caviar also cherish the tea served with it.
explanation.walkthrough: Caviar is fish roe, so 'Caviar places, perhaps' means places where fish eggs are raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A hatchery is where fish eggs are incubated, so sturgeon roe could be produced at such establishments.

clue.text: Plenty locally loathe to replace cold son of Cain

indicators.note: locally flags a dialect word for loathe
to replace means one letter of the biblical name is swapped out for the dialect word

blocks.note: Enoch was the eldest son of Cain in Genesis
C is the abbreviation for cold, the letter removed
ug is a dialect verb meaning to loathe or dread

explanation.surface: A biblical figure who loathes the cold has had his fill of it.
explanation.walkthrough: UG takes the place of the C in ENOCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty and sufficiency mean the same quantity: as much as is required, with nothing lacking.

clue.text: No more tarry over your rambling?

blocks.note: leng is an obsolete word for tarry, hence 'no more'
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Someone tells a rambling speaker to stop lingering over the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places one piece above the other in this down entry. 'No more' marks the word as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambling speech goes on too long and wanders, so it is tediously long-winded.

clue.text: Bounding from enclosure, for instance, northern river meadow

blocks.note: enc. is the abbreviation for enclosure on a letter
as introduces an example, such as
an ing is a meadow beside a river in northern English dialect

explanation.surface: An animal leaps out of its pen into a riverside field up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounding' suggests leaping; here it means forming a boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Bounding a thing means forming its limits, and enclosing it completely within a case does exactly that.

clue.text: Mollusc is round and very fresh according to fishmonger

blocks.note: a round shape looks like the letter O
a fishmonger's freshest stock is still alive

explanation.surface: A fishmonger boasts that a shellfish is plump and straight from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive shell is a sea snail with a smooth glossy shell, a genuine marine gastropod species.

clue.text: Calves of independent Kansas

blocks.note: o' is a shortened form of of
I is the abbreviation for independent
KS is the postal code of the US state

explanation.surface: Young cattle from a free state in the Midwest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calves' looks like young cattle or legs; here it means louts. Oik is British slang for an ill-mannered lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A calf can mean a stupid or loutish fellow, so the plural matches yobs or boorish people.

clue.text: Hot milk from France on top? You’ll find Scots unwilling.

indicators.note: on top in a down entry means the French word sits above the letter for hot

blocks.note: lait is French for milk
H is the abbreviation for hot, on taps

explanation.surface: A French café serves hot milk with something on top, but the Scots won't touch it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on top' puts the French word above the H in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Laith is the Scots form of loath, meaning reluctant or disinclined to do something.

clue.text: Lusitanian, say, is popular detaining discredited secret policeman

indicators.note: detaining means holding someone inside, so the policeman is held within the word for popular

blocks.note: the first letter of in, meaning popular
Lavrentiy Beria was Stalin's disgraced secret police chief
the rest of in, meaning popular

explanation.surface: A Portuguese is famous for locking up a disgraced Soviet police chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusitania was the Roman province roughly matching Portugal, which lies on the Iberian peninsula; 'say' marks an example.

clue.text: To want female out is perfidious

indicators.note: out means the letter for female is removed from the phrase

blocks.note: to feel like something is to want it
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Wishing to throw a woman out is treacherous behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Being slippery like an eel describes someone untrustworthy and evasive, hence treacherous or perfidious.

clue.text: Without causing desire Vienna Blue bucks

indicators.note: a horse that bucks throws everything about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: the ten letters of the two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A shade called Vienna Blue fails to excite anyone, perhaps a paint or fashion colour nobody wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that arouses no envy is a position or lot nobody would wish for themselves.

clue.text: Poet’s straightaway polled about going into unit

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for hornless is read backwards
going into means placed inside the word for unit

blocks.note: nott is an old word for hornless, as polled cattle are
an ace is a one, a single unit, at cards or dice

explanation.surface: A poet wants a vote counted immediately about some unit.
explanation.walkthrough: TTON goes into A_CE to give ATTONCE, Spenser's spelling of 'at once', hence 'Poet's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser's spelling of a phrase meaning immediately or without delay; the poet tag marks the archaic literary form.

clue.text: Gig informally such as the WI do if not singing Jerusalem

definitions.text: such as the WI do if not singing Jerusalem

blocks.note: first meaning: an unrehearsed musical get-together

blocks.clueFragment: such as the WI do if not singing Jerusalem
blocks.note: second meaning: a meeting spent making preserves

explanation.walkthrough: The WI is Britain's Women's Institute, famous for preserves and for singing the hymn Jerusalem at meetings, hence 'Jam and Jerusalem'.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal improvised performance by musicians, and also literally a gathering devoted to making fruit preserves.

clue.text: Mostly vague gossip about Cotter primarily being Rab C’s shadow

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the word for vague gossip is kept
primarily points to the first letter of the surname before it
about means the gossip word goes round the single letter

blocks.note: a sough is a vague rumour or murmur; its last letter is dropped
the first letter of Cotter

explanation.surface: Hazy rumours swirl about a man called Cotter shadowing Rab C. Nesbitt.
explanation.walkthrough: Rab C. Nesbitt is a Glaswegian character from a BBC Scotland comedy, so his shadow is a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, scoug means shelter or shade, so it serves as the Glaswegian word for a shadow or shadowed place.

clue.text: Excepting both leads soundly vocal of the stars

indicators.note: excepting both leads means each of the two words loses its opening letter

blocks.note: to sleep soundly is to be fast asleep
vocal and oral both mean spoken

explanation.surface: A singer is told to drop both lead parts and still sound vocal.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral is the adjective relating to stars, from the Latin astrum, as in astral bodies and astral projection.

clue.text: Rough tough giving nothing away

indicators.note: giving away nothing means the letter shaped like a zero is removed
rough treatment knocks the remaining letters out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hard man who gives nothing away under questioning.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the O (nothing) from TOUGH and rearrange; the whole clue also describes a tight-lipped hard man.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent ruffian is a rough, a tough, and the type who refuses to tell police anything.

clue.text: Fish dish is back full of mash I creamed

indicators.note: back means the little word is is read the other way
creamed means beaten up, as in cooking, so these letters are mixed
full of means the turned word holds the mixed letters inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written as the fodder

explanation.surface: A cook reports on a fish course loaded with creamed mashed potato.
explanation.walkthrough: SI wraps around ASHIM, the rearranged MASH I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashimi is the Japanese dish of thinly sliced raw fish served without rice.

clue.text: In retirement Holmes was one — a tickler of the ivories (note’s right)

indicators.note: note's right means the musical note letter becomes the letter for right

blocks.note: tickling the ivories is playing the piano
N is the abbreviation for note
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes in retirement, pictured as a pianist.
explanation.walkthrough: In Conan Doyle's stories, Holmes retired to the Sussex Downs to keep bees. Swap the N of A PIANIST for R.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper keeps hives, and Conan Doyle's detective retired to Sussex to study and keep bees.

clue.text: Anonymous book’s about hotel receptions

indicators.note: about means the books go round the letter for hotel

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for anonymous
a tome is a book; book's read as book is gives the plural
H is hotel in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An unsigned book is about hotel parties.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes in after the T of TOMES.
explanation.definitionFit: An at-home is an informal party or reception held in one's house on a stated day, so the plural is receptions.

clue.text: What crop top reveals lifted lacklustre figure

indicators.note: lifted in a down entry means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

blocks.note: something lacklustre is dim
a riff is a repeated musical figure

explanation.surface: A dull figure is lifted up by a cropped top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figure' looks like body shape; here it is a musical phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A crop top is a short shirt that leaves the stomach area bare, exposing the belly between chest and waist.

clue.text: With it inquire after fluid?

blocks.note: with it means fashionable, hip
FL is the abbreviation for fluid, as in fl oz
to inquire is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether there is anything to drink about.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the person carrying this item, fashionable and asking where the drink is.
explanation.definitionFit: A hip flask is the small pocket bottle for spirits, the thing you carry when liquid refreshment is the question.

clue.text: Talent is not working around college

indicators.note: around means the broken word surrounds the letter for college

blocks.note: the first part of faulty, meaning not working
C is the abbreviation for college
the rest of faulty, meaning not working

explanation.surface: A talented person is out of work around the college.
explanation.definitionFit: A faculty is a natural ability or power of mind, such as a gift or knack for something.

clue.text: New dignitary rejecting first order of flowers

indicators.note: rejecting first means the opening letter of the official is thrown out
new means made over, so the remaining letters take a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A newly appointed dignitary turns down the first order of flowers, perhaps for a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' looks like a florist's purchase; here it is the botanical rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Trigynia was a Linnaean classification grouping plants whose blooms have three pistils, a botanical order.

clue.text: Previously more attractive American and knight in row

indicators.note: in means the two abbreviations sit inside the word for row

blocks.note: the first letter of tier, a row
A is the abbreviation for American
K is knight in chess notation
the rest of tier, a row

explanation.surface: An American and a knight once looked better seated in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previously' marks an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Taky is an old adjective meaning attractive or taking, and the comparative form means more charming or appealing.

clue.text: Baroness in Barcelona buried tangle, say

blocks.note: to bury something is to hide it
tangle is a kind of seaweed, which is an alga

explanation.surface: A Spanish noblewoman has hidden away some mess or snarl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks tangle as one example of an alga, not a knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidalga is a Spanish noblewoman of lesser rank, the female counterpart of a hidalgo.

clue.text: Acting leader of Labour sitting on heaps to ration

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the party name
sitting on in a down entry puts the first pieces above the word for heaps

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for acting
the first letter of Labour
a lot means heaps

explanation.surface: The acting Labour leader sits on piles of food for rationing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sitting on' places the first pieces above LOT in this down entry. Labour is a British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: To ration is to distribute fixed portions, and allotting means apportioning or assigning shares.

clue.text: A key ligature

blocks.note: taken as written
Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: A single key that joins or binds things together.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesc is the Old English name for the joined letter ae, a typographic ligature of two vowels.

clue.text: End first hint of corruption with no trouble

indicators.note: first hint of means just the opening letter of the word

blocks.note: the first letter of corruption
ease means without difficulty

explanation.surface: Stamp out the first sign of corruption easily.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to stop or halt it, which is a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Old and surprisingly early neckerchief used by Burns?

indicators.note: surprisingly means turning out unexpectedly, so the letters land in an unexpected order

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
the five letters of early rearranged

explanation.surface: An old scarf turns up surprisingly early, the kind a poet might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Burns wrote in Scots, so the question mark flags a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots an o'erlay is a cravat or neck covering, literally a thing laid over the throat.

clue.text: Restaurateur shows a distinctive character

indicators.note: shows means the letters are on display inside the word before it

blocks.note: inside resta-ura-teur, from the fourth letter

explanation.surface: A restaurant owner reveals a distinctive personality.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is the distinctive atmosphere or quality that seems to surround a person or place.

clue.text: Arbitrary decree from King about entering service

indicators.note: entering means going inside the word for service

blocks.note: the first part of use, which means service
K is the chess abbreviation for king
A is an abbreviation for about
the rest of use, which means service

explanation.surface: A king issues a high-handed order about how servants should work.
explanation.walkthrough: K and A go together inside USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was an edict of the Russian tsar, so by extension any high-handed order imposed without consultation.

clue.text: Levy one literally caught by overturning point

indicators.note: overturning means turning the word for point back to front
caught by means held inside the turned word

blocks.note: to point at something is to aim at it
I is the Roman numeral one
lit. is the abbreviation for literally

explanation.surface: One person is literally caught in a point that gets overturned, like a tax levy reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy is a body of troops raised or conscripted, which is what a citizen militia is.

clue.text: Engineering end of trees? Actually made a swathe of them

indicators.note: engineering means constructing anew, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: all ten letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Is someone plotting the end of trees? No, they actually planted swathes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of trees' looks like a selection signal for a last letter, but all three words are the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To enforest is to convert land into woodland, so it means covering an area with a great swathe of planted trees.

clue.text: Maybe tête-à-tête involving tense student of theology

indicators.note: involving means the furniture word wraps around the grammar letter

blocks.note: a tête-à-tête is an S-shaped two-seat sofa, maybe meaning an example
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A private, tense chat between two people about theology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tête-à-tête' looks like a conversation; here it is the piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A softa is a Muslim student of theology and sacred law in Turkey, attached to a mosque school.

clue.text: Awkwardly tense getting about your hydrocarbon

indicators.note: awkwardly means clumsily arranged, so these letters are jumbled
getting about means the jumbled letters go round the short word

blocks.note: taken as written as the fodder
yr is the written abbreviation of your

explanation.surface: An awkwardly tense moment involving your fuel or chemicals.
explanation.definitionFit: Styrene is an aromatic compound of carbon and hydrogen, the liquid monomer that makes polystyrene.
